what: E4a: the warning operating point on STORED forecasts (nothing is trained). Written by code/20_warning_policy.py on 2026-10-28.
status: EXPERIMENT (28-29 Oct 2026): every trigger chosen on the validation years; test years scored once per rule

design.what_is_chosen_where: every trigger (a multiple of the basin's Q95, from the grid) and every stacker cut is chosen on the validation years of the set's own split; the test years are scored once per rule; nothing is trained

rules.csi: the trigger with the best pooled onset CSI on the validation years (the rule of scripts 16 and 18, which search the grid 0.30-1.50; this script searches 0.50-2.00, so triggers above 1.50 are reachable here; ties go to the trigger nearest 1.0)
rules.far_cap: the trigger with the most onsets warned on the validation years among those whose pooled onset false share is at or below 0.3 (the false share the GO rule allows), ties broken by the higher CSI; reached=False when none is, then the trigger with the lowest false share, ties to the larger trigger (warning_policy.choose_trigger)

design.onset: a target day whose flow `lead` days earlier (the issue day) was at or below Q95 (flood.flood_scores); at leads 2 and 3 this means 'issued while the river was low', not 'first day above Q95'
design.pooled: hits, misses and false alarms summed over the 12 basins, then POD = hits / (hits + misses), FAR = false alarms / (hits + false alarms), CSI = hits / (hits + misses + false alarms) (flood.rates)
design.seed_sets: lstm_<set>_s<i>, i in range(5), those that exist; the seed-mean set is the day-by-day average of their forecasts (checked: max_abs_difference_seed_mean_vs_average_of_seed_sets); each seed set is scored at its own validation-chosen trigger and at the seed-mean set's trigger

bootstrap.kind: block bootstrap over the target days of the test years
bootstrap.interval: 2.5th to 97.5th percentile of the pooled onset POD and FAR at the fixed trigger
bootstrap.note: blocks keep the correlation of neighbouring days and of the basins of one storm; the pattern of 18_forecast_input.py

design.average_precision: numpy, the definition of sklearn.metrics.average_precision_score: onset rows of the test years ranked by forecast / Q95, no trigger
design.stacker: warning_policy.stack: logistic regression on [log forecast/Q95 (seed mean), log today's flow/Q95, seed spread, seed max], fitted on the first half of the validation years, cut chosen on the second half by the far_cap rule; main-split sets only
design.any_lead: warning_policy.any_lead: a target day counts as warned when the issue of lead 1, 2 or 3 warned of it at that lead's trigger of the rule; onsets by the lead-1 rule

go_rule.applied_to: test years, at the warning level chosen on the validation years; separately for all high-flow days and for onsets; pooled over the 12 basins and per basin; lead 1, 2, 3; for lstm_wq, lstm_w and lstm_wqf
go_rule.definitions: pod = share of high-flow days that were warned; far = share of warnings that were false; csi = hits / (hits + misses + false alarms)

far_cap.note: no trigger of the grid keeps the onset false share at or below the cap on validation; the trigger with the lowest false share is given
no trigger of the grid keeps the onset false share at or below the cap on validation; the trigger with the lowest false share is given

outcome: At the warning level the project chose on the validation years (best CSI), the LSTM with AORC rain to midnight (an analysis made after the fact) warns of 51% of the 611 onsets 1 day ahead (hindsight at most about 3 points) with 50% of its warnings false; at the level that keeps the false share at or below 30% on the validation years it warns of 25% (test false share 30%); the perfect-rain model keeps 59% and the perfect-weather model 61% (both an upper bound that cannot be had in practice); the GO rule for the onsets (at least 70% of the onsets warned and at most 30% of the onset warnings false) is met only by the perfect weather model 2 days ahead, and there only by the seed-mean set (no single training meets it); that model is an upper bound that cannot be had in practice, and no model whose inputs can be had in practice meets it; on all high-flow days, most of them continuing floods that persistence also catches, it is met by the model with the GEFS forecast (substituted) 1 day ahead at its CSI trigger (78% warned, 27% false); the model with the GEFS forecast, retrained (own split) 1 day ahead at its CSI trigger (76% warned, 27% false); a decision layer re-arranges the trade-off and does not create skill.
outcome_caveat: Single networks (the three seeds of the rain-to-midnight set, each at the set's trigger): 49%-55% warned with 51%-57% false at the CSI level, 23%-28% with 28%-34% false at the 30%-false level; a block bootstrap over the test days (30-day blocks, 2000 draws) puts the seed-mean set's share at 47%-56% and 21%-28% at the two levels. The logistic stacker (fitted on the first half of the validation years, cut chosen on the second half at the 30% cap) warns of 24% at 29% false for the rain-to-midnight set and 27% at 24% false for the forecast set (against 14% at its 30%-false trigger). Warned by any lead (1, 2 or 3 days before) with the CSI triggers: 59% of the onsets at 85% false; 45 of the 298 lead-1 misses of the rain-to-midnight set were warned two or three days before. No trigger of the grid kept the validation false share at or below 30% for lstm_wqaF_sub l2, lstm_wqaF_sub l3: the lowest-false trigger is reported there. The satellite-era split's numbers are comparable only inside that split.
